HarmonicFrequency · HzAmplitude

How this experiment works—and where it can fail

A YIN-style repetition detector estimates pitch in overlapping 80 ms frames (60–600 Hz). A Hann-windowed FFT measures energy near harmonic multiples. Median strengths from a steady section set 24 sine-wave amplitudes. Shared-pitch mode interpolates the spectral envelope onto a new harmonic grid; it does not simply double all frequencies.

This is a research-inspired harmonic approximation, not a trained AI voice model. It does not identify vowel letters, copy your full voice, or reconstruct the opening glide in 유. Noise, multiple voices, unstable pitch, octave errors, and sparse harmonics can cause failure. The periodicity score measures repetition, not correctness. If the estimate sounds an octave too high or low, inspect the spectrum and try another section.

Background: YIN pitch estimation (2002) · Sinusoidal and spectral synthesis. Modern DDSP vocal synthesis research (2023) uses trained models; this feature uses deterministic pitch and Fourier analysis.

LIVE SPECTRUM · LEVEL / FREQUENCY

Waiting for microphone input
Try humming a steady note, then speaking. A steady pitched sound often creates regularly spaced harmonic peaks; speech changes over time. Spectrum levels are relative digital levels (dBFS), not calibrated sound-pressure measurements. Auto waveform scale magnifies quiet input, so use a fixed scale when comparing amplitudes.

Live analysis and recordings stay in this browser; no audio is uploaded. Recordings are kept temporarily until you download them, start a new take, or close this page. Microphone monitoring is muted to prevent feedback. Stop releases the microphone; switching away from this page also stops it. Use headphones if you play generated tones during microphone analysis.

Signal: Σ amplitude × sin(2π × frequency × time). Audio is scaled by the sum of active amplitudes to prevent clipping; plots show the original relative amplitudes. At wide time scales, dense waves appear as envelopes.
